expected_issues.title: Minor wording consistency: nearby metrics use both “thread pool” and “threadpool”
expected_issues.description:
Minor wording consistency: nearby metrics use both “thread pool” and “threadpool”. Consider using one style consistently (e.g., “thread pool”) in these new descriptions to match most surrounding strings and improve readability/searchability.

```suggestion
    M(PolygonDictionaryThreads, "Number of threads in the thread pool for polygon dictionaries.") \
    M(PolygonDictionaryThreadsActive, "Number of active threads in the thread pool for polygon dictionaries.") \
    M(PolygonDictionaryThreadsScheduled, "Number of queued or active jobs in the thread pool for polygon dictionaries.") \
```

expected_issues.title: The variables `initial_thread` and `initial_thread_group` are initialized once and never…
expected_issues.description:
The variables `initial_thread` and `initial_thread_group` are initialized once and never changed. They should be marked as `const` to clearly communicate their immutability and prevent accidental modification. This improves code safety and readability.

```suggestion
#ifdef DEBUG_OR_SANITIZER_BUILD
            DB::ThreadStatus * const initial_thread = DB::current_thread;
            const DB::ThreadGroupPtr initial_thread_group = DB::CurrentThread::getGroup();
#endif
```

expected_issues.title: Throwing an exception from a thread-pool worker after executing a job can call std::termi…
expected_issues.description:
Throwing an exception from a thread-pool worker after executing a job can call std::terminate if it propagates out of the worker loop (common for std::thread entrypoints). Even in DEBUG builds, this can crash the whole process during testing. Consider turning this into a non-throwing diagnostic (e.g., LOG_FATAL/abort with clearer intent, or ASSERT with controlled handling), or ensure the worker catches DB::Exception and reports it without unwinding past the thread entry.

Also, the check compares ThreadGroupPtr by pointer identity; if getGroup() can return different shared_ptr instances referring to the same underlying group, this may false-positive. Prefer comparing a stable identifier (e.g., master_thread_id) when both non-null.

expected_issues.title: This new restriction may break existing valid usages: `PoolT` could be `GlobalThreadPool`…
expected_issues.description:
This new restriction may break existing valid usages: `PoolT` could be `GlobalThreadPool` via alias/typedef or `const GlobalThreadPool` etc. If the intent is to forbid scheduling on the global pool, consider covering cv/ref qualifiers (e.g., `std::remove_cvref_t<PoolT>`) to avoid bypassing the check accidentally.

```suggestion
    static_assert(!std::is_same_v<std::remove_cvref_t<PoolT>, GlobalThreadPool>,
        "Scheduling tasks directly on GlobalThreadPool is not allowed because it doesn't set up CurrentThread. "
        "Create a new ThreadPool (local or in SharedThreadPools.h) or use ThreadFromGlobalPool.");
```

expected_issues.title: Potential behavior change: `ThreadGroupSwitcher` only calls `setThreadName` when `thread_…
expected_issues.description:
Potential behavior change: `ThreadGroupSwitcher` only calls `setThreadName` when `thread_name` is non-empty. Passing empty string here likely leaves the worker thread name unchanged, making debugging/profiling harder vs the previous code path (which at least didn’t set a name either, but other call sites now set names). Consider providing a meaningful name (e.g. "DistrOnFinish"/"DistrFinish") or explicitly documenting why empty is desired.

Also confirm `allow_existing_group` default (=false) is correct for thread-pool jobs here; if this lambda can run on a thread that is already attached to another group, it may assert/LOGICAL_ERROR. If that situation is possible, pass `allow_existing_group=true` to restore the previous group on exit.
expected_issues.source_text:

Consider providing a meaningful name (e.g. "DistrOnFinish"/"DistrFinish") or explicitly documenting why empty is desired.

Also confirm `allow_existing_group` default (=false) is correct for thread-pool jobs here; if this lambda can run on a thread that is already attached to another group, it may assert/LOGICAL_ERROR. If that situation is possible, pass `allow_existing_group=true` to restore the previous group on exit.

known_false_positives.description:
Creating a `ThreadPool` instance locally within a recursive function is highly inefficient. This constructs a new thread pool (and potentially spawns threads) for every internal node of the polygon structure, even when `depth > kMultiProcessingDepth` where it is not used. This can lead to significant performance overhead and resource exhaustion (e.g., creating 128 threads for every node). 

Suggestion: Instantiate the `ThreadPool` once at the top-level entry point and pass it down to `makeCell` by reference, or revert to using `GlobalThreadPool` if appropriate. Also, ensure the pool is only used when `depth <= kMultiProcessingDepth`.
ThreadGroupSwitcher destructor marked noexcept may be problematic if cleanup operations could potentially throw exceptions during stack unwinding.
